Surah Al-Insan (Al-Insan [Human]) [Meccan or Medinan; its verses number thirty-one]

﴿Has there come upon man﴾ (Adam) ﴿a period of time﴾ forty years ﴿when he was not a thing worthy of mention﴾ during which he was a figure shaped from clay that was not mentioned. Or, what is meant by "man" is the human species, and by "a period of time" the duration of gestation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, We created man﴾ (al-insan), the species, ﴿from a drop of mingled fluid﴾ (nutfah amshaj), mixtures, meaning from the fluid of the man and the fluid of the woman, mixed and blended together, ﴿We test him﴾ (nabtalih), We examine him through the obligations (al-taklif), and the sentence is either a new statement (mustaanifah) or a circumstantial clause (hal muqaddarah), meaning intending to test him when he becomes fit for it, ﴿so We made him﴾ (fa-ja'alnahu), because of that.

Translation of the Tafsir al-Jalalayn commentary on Surah 76 (al-Insan), verse 3:

﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way.﴾ We made clear to him the path of guidance by sending the messengers. ﴿Either grateful﴾ i.e., believing, ﴿or ungrateful.﴾ These two are circumstantial clauses (ḥāl, pl. aḥwāl) referring to the object (the pronoun "him"), meaning: We made the way clear to him in his state of either gratitude or disbelief, which is predetermined (for him). Or "either... or" is for the detailing of the states.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 76, verse 4:

﴿Indeed, We have prepared﴾ (i.e., readied) ﴿for the disbelievers chains﴾ by which they will be dragged in the Fire, ﴿and shackles﴾ around their necks, to which the chains are fastened, ﴿and a blaze﴾ (sa'ir), a fire kindled to a blaze, meaning inflamed, by which they will be tormented.

Surah 76, verse 5 (Tafsir al-Jalalayn):

﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾ (al-abrar), the plural of barr or barr (bar), those who are obedient, ﴿will drink from a cup﴾, which is the vessel of wine (ka's), with the wine in it. The intended meaning of "cup" here is "wine," a case of naming the contained by the container (tasmiyat al-hal bi-ism al-mahall), and "min" (from) is for partitive meaning (li-l-tab'id). ﴿Its mixture will be﴾ (kana mizajuha), that is, what it is mixed with.

﴿A spring﴾, a substitute for "camphor", whose fragrance is in it. ﴿From which the servants of Allah drink﴾, that is, His friends, ﴿making it gush forth in abundance﴾, that is, they lead it wherever they wish from their dwellings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 7:

﴿They fulfil the vow﴾ in obedience to Allah, ﴿and fear a Day whose evil is widespread﴾ spreading far and wide.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 8:

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive.﴾ That is, "the food" and their desire for it. ﴿The needy﴾: the poor. ﴿The orphan﴾: one who has no father. ﴿And the captive﴾: meaning the one imprisoned by right.

﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah﴾, seeking His reward, ﴿We do not want from you recompense or thanks﴾. *Shukran* (thanks), in which is the *'illa* (underlying reason) for the feeding. Did they say this, or did Allah know it from them so that He praised them for it? There are two opinions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 10:

﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day of frowning, ﴾ [in which faces will be contorted] meaning, dreadful in appearance because of its severity, ﴿extremely distressing.﴾ [meaning, severe in that respect].
﴿So Allah protected them from the evil of that Day and gave them﴾ — He gave them ﴿radiance﴾, beauty and brightness in their faces.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 12:

﴿And He will reward them for their patience with a garden and silk.﴾ For their patience in refraining from disobedience, [He will give them] a garden [which] they will enter, and silk [which] they will wear.

﴿Reclining﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of the nominative (marfūʿ) subject of the implied verb "adkhalūhā" (they entered it). ﴿Therein, upon couches﴾: the thrones (al-surar) within the canopied enclosures (al-ḥijāl). ﴿They see not﴾: they do not find, is a second circumstantial qualifier. ﴿Therein any sun, nor any bitter cold﴾: neither scorching heat nor cold. It is said that az-zamharīr is the moon, so it is radiant without sun or moon.

Translation of the passage:

﴿Wa-dāniyatan﴾ (and near) — close, conjoined grammatically to the place of "they will not see." That is, they will not see [the sun] — ﴿upon them﴾ from it (the sun) — ﴿its shade﴾, its trees. ﴿And its clusters hung low, lowered in readiness﴾ — its fruits were brought near, so that the one standing, the one sitting, and the one reclining can reach them.
﴿And there will be circulated among them﴾ therein ﴿vessels of silver and cups﴾, meaning goblets (aqdāḥ) without handles.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 16:

﴿Glass vessels of silver﴾, meaning: they are of silver, whose inner part is visible from the outside, like glass. ﴿They shall determine its measure﴾, meaning: those who go around (the attendants). ﴿Determining it precisely﴾, according to the measure that quenches the drinkers' thirst, neither more nor less, and that is the most delightful of drinks.
﴿And they will be given to drink therein a cup﴾ [of wine] ﴿whose mixture was﴾ that with which it is mixed ﴿ginger.﴾ Meaning: its water is like the ginger which the Arabs enjoy.
ʿAynan (a spring) is a substitute (badal) for zanjabilan (ginger). ﴿A spring therein called Salsabil.﴾ (Meaning) smooth and easy to swallow in the throat.

And there will go around among them young boys of perpetual youth (﴿ويطوف عليهم ولدان مخلدون﴾). By the attribute of the boys: they never grow old (﴿لا يشيبون﴾). ﴿إذا رأيتهم حسبتهم﴾: because of their beauty and their dispersal in service. ﴿لؤلؤا منثورا﴾: (you think them to be) scattered pearls, either from the string (that holds them) or from the shell, and (the pearl) is more beautiful than them in other respects.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 76, verse 20:

﴿And when you look there﴾, i.e., when sight reaches you in Paradise, ﴿you will see﴾ is the response to "when," ﴿bliss﴾ that cannot be described, ﴿and a great kingdom﴾, vast, with no limit to it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 21:

﴿Upon them﴾ above them; it is accusative as an adverb of place, and it is the predicate of a subject that follows it. In another reading, with the yā' silent, it is a subject, and what follows it is the predicate, and the attached pronoun refers to those who are mentioned before them. ﴿Garments of green silk﴾ (ḥarīr, silk). ﴿Green﴾ with a nominative ending (rafʿ). ﴿And brocade﴾ with a genitive ending (jarr); it is the thicker kind of dībāj (brocade), so it is the lining (baṭāʾin), while al-sundus is the outer layer (ẓahāʾir). In another reading the case-endings of these two words are reversed, in another both are nominative, and in another both are genitive. ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾, and in another place of gold, to indicate that they will be adorned with both kinds together and separately. ﴿And their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink﴾, an intensification of its purity and cleanliness, unlike the wine of this world.
﴿Indeed, this﴾ bliss

﴿إنا نحن﴾ *tawkid* (emphasis) for the noun of *inna* (the particle of emphasis), or a *fasl* (separating pronoun) ﴿Indeed, We, ...﴾ ﴿نزلنا عليك القرآن تنزيلا﴾ is the predicate of *inna*, meaning: ﴿We have sent down to you the Qur'an, sending it down in stages﴾, i.e., We revealed it in parts and did not send it down all at once.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 24:

﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾ — that is, in conveying His message. ﴿And do not obey from among them⁠ ⁠a sinner or a disbeliever⁠﴾ — that is, from among the disbelievers, namely ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Turn away from this matter." It is also permissible that the verse means every sinner and every disbeliever, i.e., do not obey either of them, whoever they may be, in whatever they call you to of sin or disbelief.

ظ‹ï»؟**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 25:**

﴿And mention the name of your Lord﴾ in the prayer ﴿at dawn and at dusk﴾; it means the dawn prayer (Fajr), the noon prayer (Dhuhr), and the afternoon prayer (ʿAsr).

[Qur'an 76:26] "And during the night, prostrate to Him, and glorify Him through a long part of the night."

(Tafsir al-Jalalayn) "And during the night, prostrate to Him" means the maghrib (sunset) and the 'isha' (night) prayers. "And glorify Him through a long part of the night" means: perform the voluntary prayer (tatawwu') in it, as was mentioned earlier, for two-thirds of it, or half of it, or a third of it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 76, verse 27:

﴿Indeed, these people love the hasty life﴾ (al-dunya, the worldly life), ﴿and leave behind them a heavy day﴾, meaning severe, that is the Day of Resurrection, for which they do not work.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 28:

﴿We created them and strengthened their frames﴾ (we made strong) ﴿their joints﴾ (their limbs and joints), ﴿and whenever We will, We can replace﴾ (We can make) ﴿their like﴾ in creation, as substitutes for them, by destroying them ﴿with a complete replacement﴾ (for emphasis). And "idha" (whenever) has been placed in the position of "in" (if), as in ﴿if He wills, He can take you away﴾, because He, exalted is He, did not will that; and "idha" is used for what does not occur.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 76, verse 29:

﴿Indeed, this﴾ surah ﴿is a reminder﴾, an admonition for creation, ﴿so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾, a path, through obedience.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 76, verse 30:

﴿And you do not will﴾ (read with the taa' and the yaa', i.e. "you" or "they") taking the path through obedience, ﴿except that God wills﴾ it. ﴿Indeed God is ever Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿Wise﴾ in His action.

He admits whomever He wills into His mercy, that is, His Paradise, and they are the believers. And the wrongdoers (al-zalimin) is in the accusative because of a verb implied and omitted, meaning "He has prepared" (a'adda), which is explained by what follows: ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾, painful (mu'lim), and they are the disbelievers.
